login.title: Sign in
login.lede: Sign in with the email and password the owner gave you.

home.lede: This is where every rupee sits right now: each site’s profit, then what the firms hold, owe and are owed.
home.ledeSupervisor: What you spend at the site goes on the daily report. Stock that arrives goes under Stock.
home.todayHint: Each part of the report for each of your sites. Tap a site to fill what is missing.
home.noSites: No site is given to you yet. Ask the owner to add one in People.
home.emptyHint: Start in Setup: add your firms, sites, parties, clients and bank accounts. Then add the first bill on a party’s or client’s page.
home.emptySupervisor: Nothing here yet. When the office gives you cash, it shows up here.

masters.readOnly: Only the owner can change these.
masters.lede: The lists the forms pick from: firms, sites, parties and clients, contracts, bank or cash accounts, materials and GST rates.

delete.title: Delete
delete.warning: For something added by mistake. It goes to the recycle bin (Admin → Recycle bin) and can be put back for 30 days. Anything that entries, reports, bank accounts or staff logins still use cannot be deleted: switch it off instead, and it stops showing in the lists.
delete.wrongName: The name typed does not match. Nothing was deleted.
delete.binned: Moved to the recycle bin. The owner can put it back from Admin → Recycle bin for 30 days.
delete.noFirm: A firm cannot be deleted: every entry, site and account belongs to one. It can only be renamed.
delete.inUse: Can’t delete: it is still used by {what}. Switch it off instead.

usedBy.user_firms: staff logins (remove it from the person in People first)
usedBy.user_sites: staff logins (remove it from the person in People first)
usedBy.stock_in: stock that arrived (remove those lines on Stock → Arrived first)
usedBy.mix_items: combination works (take it out of them in Setup → Combination works first)
usedBy.parties: workers or staff given this site
usedBy.has_months: pay saved in Labour payment months
usedBy.salary_months: days and salary typed on Salary → Skill

fields.name: Name
fields.rate_paise: Rate (₹) — daily report price per hour for a worker, salary per month for staff
fields.from_date: Counts from (the month of this date on)
fields.runs_labour: Runs Labour payment and owns the AJAX machines (one firm)

money_reason.deposit_back_client: Security deposit released by a client
money_reason.party_back: Cheque returned / money back from a party
money_reason.client_back: Cheque returned / money back to a client

users.title: Users
users.keepPassword: Leave the password empty to keep it.

history.title: Change log
history.lede: Every change to Setup and People: who made it, when, and what it was before.
history.testDelete: Deleted with the secret key (before the recycle bin)

errors.not_allowed: You are not allowed to do this.
errors.inactive: This account is switched off. Ask the owner.
errors.other_firm: This belongs to the other firm. Switch firm at the top right first.
errors.duplicate_bill: This bill number is already in the books for this party. Cancel that entry first if it was wrong
errors.account_needs_firm: Every bank and cash account belongs to one firm. Choose it.
errors.future_date: This date is in the future. Money is written down on the day it moves.
errors.invalid_gstin: A GST number has 15 characters, like 27AAAAA0000A1Z5. Check it against the paper.
errors.method_account: Online and cheque come from a bank account. Cash comes from a cash account.
errors.maybe_repeat: This looks like one already saved
errors.one_cash: This firm already has its Cash. A firm has one Cash and any number of banks.
errors.is_firm: This is one of our own firms. It is already on the Pay and Receive lists.

common.unsaved: What you typed is not saved yet. Leave without saving?

plain.clientAdvance: Advance from {client} to {firm} · work still owed
plain.excess: Extra cash found at day close

money.title: Money we hold
money.hint: Bank accounts and cash in hand.

betweenFirms.title: Between our firms
betweenFirms.hint: What our own firms owe each other. Open Between firms for each account.

heldByClients.title: Held by clients
heldByClients.hint: Still our money. It comes back later.

gst.title: GST
gst.hint: GST paid on party bills, to claim back, and GST charged on client bills, to pay.

owner.title: Owner
owner.hint: The owner’s own money, old balances and cash differences.

sites.title: Sites
sites.hint: Profit = billed to the client − all costs, from every firm.

tds.title: TDS
tds.hint: TDS deducted from party bills, to pay to the government.

assets.title: Company assets
assets.hint: Tools and other things bought to reuse at any site; not a site’s cost.

unknown.title: Not yet known
unknown.hint: Money that came in or went out and is still to be sorted out. Open the Bankbook.

firm.title: Firm costs and income
firm.hint: Salary and wages paid, office costs, bank charges, and other income. Not part of any site’s profit.

new.title: What happened?
new.lede: Pick what happened. You fill in a short form; the app does the accounting.

entries.cancelHint: Nothing is deleted. The app adds an exact opposite entry, so the history stays.

bin.title: Recycle bin
bin.lede: What was deleted in the last 30 days, and who deleted it. Put anything back as it was; after 30 days it is gone for good.
bin.name: Name
bin.actions: Put back or delete for good
bin.empty: The bin is empty. Anything deleted shows here for 30 days.

errors.duplicate: It could not be put back: something with the same name has been added since. Rename that one first.
errors.missing_link: It could not be put back: the unit, site or other record it belonged to has been deleted since. Put that back first.
errors.not_restored: It could not be put back. Nothing was changed.
errors.not_purged: It could not be deleted. Nothing was changed.

demo.title: Clear demo data
demo.lede: Before handing the app over: every record with test or demo in its name, ready to go to the recycle bin in one go. Untick anything to keep. Firms are never deleted, and neither are bills or payments: a demo account they use stays, and is listed after.
demo.typeConfirm: To clear the ticked records, type CONFIRM
demo.none: Nothing named test or demo is left. To clear a record here, give it test or demo in its name.
demo.moved: {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} went to the recycle bin: {names}.
demo.kept: {count, plural, one {# record was} other {# records were}} kept because something real still uses them:
demo.keptHint: Switch these off instead, and they stop showing in the lists.

daybook.lede: Every bill and payment, day by day, newest first. Tap a name to see the entry. The totals are on the Dashboard.
daybook.siteLede: What this site has billed and spent, and every entry for it.
daybook.sitesHintFirm: Only this firm’s share. Profit = billed − costs.
daybook.costsHint: Costs at this site, by kind of work.

vendor-bill.title: Bill from a party
vendor-bill.when: A party sent a bill for material, machines or work.
vendor-bill.what: The site’s cost goes up by the bill before GST. The GST is kept apart: the firm claims it back. If TDS is deducted, it is kept apart too: it is owed to the government, so the party is paid less. The firm owes the party the total less TDS, even before anyone pays. Paying it later is a separate entry: “Pay a party”. What arrived at the site is added to its stock by the supervisor, not here.

hints.firm_id: The firm named on the bill.
hints.vendor_id: Not in the list? Add them in Setup → Parties.
hints.site_id: Where the material or work was used.
hints.bill_no: The number printed on the party’s bill.
hints.narration: Anything worth remembering, e.g. “40 bags cement”.
hints.tds_rate: Left empty, no TDS is deducted. The rate is worked out on the bill before GST.

pay-vendor.title: Pay a party
pay-vendor.when: Money went to a party by bank, UPI or cash.
pay-vendor.what: What the firm owes the party goes down, and the bank or cash goes down by the same amount. The site’s cost does not change: it was counted when the bill came. If one firm’s bank pays another firm’s bill, the app notes that the second firm now owes the first.

hints.firm_id: The firm whose bill this pays.
hints.from_account_id: The bank or cash the money left from.
hints.reference: Optional. Fill it in when you have it: it helps match the bank statement later.
hints.payment_method: Online or cheque: the firm’s bank. Cash: the firm’s cash.

client-bill.title: Bill to a client
client-bill.when: We sent a client a bill for work done.
client-bill.what: The work done (the bill before GST) counts as the site’s income. The GST on top is owed to the government. The client owes us the total after TDS, retention and security deposit; those are still our money, just held for now.

hints.work_order_id: The contract this bill is for.
hints.retention: Leave empty if the client keeps no retention. Worked out on the bill before GST.
hints.security_deposit: Leave empty if the client keeps no security deposit.
hints.tds_rate: Leave empty if the client deducts no TDS. Worked out on the bill before GST.

client-receipt.title: Money from a client
client-receipt.what: Money in the bank goes up, and what the client owes us goes down. Profit does not change: it was earned when the work was billed.

hints.reference: Optional. Fill it in when you have it: it helps match the bank statement later.
hints.payment_method: Online or cheque: the firm’s bank. Cash: the firm’s cash.

site-spend.title: Spent at a site
site-spend.when: Cash was spent at a site: labour, small material, diesel, tea…
site-spend.what: The site’s cost goes up and the cash in hand goes down by the same amount.

hints.narration: What was bought or paid for, e.g. “12 helpers, 1 day”.
hints.paid_to_id: Pick the person or shop if they are in the list.
hints.material_id: If you bought a material (cement, sand…), pick it here. The type then fills in by itself.

owner-money.title: Owner’s money
owner-money.when: The owner put personal money into the business, or took some out.
owner-money.what: Money the owner puts in is not income, and money taken out is not a site cost. Both are recorded as the owner’s own money, so site profits stay true.

move-money.title: Move money
move-money.when: Money moved between our own accounts: bank to petty cash, cash to the bank, cash to a person.
move-money.what: One account goes down and the other goes up by the same amount. It is not spending, so no cost changes.

not-yet-known.title: Money not yet known
not-yet-known.when: Money came in or went out and nobody knows why yet.
not-yet-known.what: It is counted in the account at once and shows in red until it is sorted out.

hints.narration: What the bank statement or cash book says about it.

other-money.title: Other money in or out
other-money.when: Office costs, bank charges, tax, loans, deposits, retention released, machine rent.
other-money.what: The account goes up or down, and the reason says where it counts. It is typed from a bankbook.

opening.title: Starting balance
opening.why: A balance carried over from the old Excel records, so the app starts where the books left off.

vendor_bill.title: Bill from a party
vendor_bill.why: The firm owes the money from the moment the bill arrives, even before paying. The cost, before GST, belongs to the site where it was used; the GST on it is claimed back, so it is not a cost. TDS deducted is owed to the government, so the party is paid less, and it is kept in the TDS record.

vendor_payment.title: Paid a party
vendor_payment.why: Paying a bill does not change the site’s cost; it was counted when the bill came. Money just moves from our bank or cash to the party.

site_cash_expense.title: Spent at a site
site_cash_expense.why: This is real spending, so it goes onto the site’s cost. The cash in hand goes down by the same amount.

client_bill.title: Bill to a client
client_bill.why: The value of the work, before GST, is income; the GST on top is collected for the government. TDS, retention and security deposit are still our money, just held by others: TDS is claimed back in the tax return, retention comes back after the defect period.

client_receipt.title: Money from a client
client_receipt.why: Being paid does not change profit. It turns “the client owes us” into money in the bank.

cash_transfer.title: Money moved
cash_transfer.why: Moving money between our own pockets is not spending. The total stays the same.

cash_close_difference.title: Cash short or extra
cash_close_difference.why: The counted cash did not match the books. The difference is recorded on its own, never slipped into another cost.

owner_capital.title: Owner put money in
owner_capital.why: Every rupee has to come from somewhere. Here it comes from the owner, so it is recorded as the owner’s money in the business.

owner_drawing.title: Owner took money out
owner_drawing.why: Recorded as the owner’s own money going out, so it never looks like a site cost.

reversal.title: Cancelling entry
reversal.why: The exact opposite of an earlier entry, so the two add up to nothing. Nothing is ever deleted: the history stays.

not_yet_known.title: Not yet known
not_yet_known.why: The money really moved, so it is counted now. Who and why are still to be found, and it stays red until they are.

firm_transfer.title: Money between our firms
firm_transfer.why: It is still our money, in another firm’s account. The firm that got it owes it, or has now been paid what it was owed.

labour_supplied.title: Labour supplied
labour_supplied.why: One of our firms gave labour to another’s site. It is that site’s cost and the supplier’s income, and no money moves until it is taken or paid.

machine_rent.title: Machine rent
machine_rent.why: One of our firms’ machines worked at another’s site. It is that site’s cost and the owner firm’s income.

wages_paid.title: Salary and wages
wages_paid.why: Money given to our people. What each one is owed is on their own account.

other_in.title: Other money in
other_in.why: Money that came in other than from a client’s bill. The reason says where it counts.

other_out.title: Other money out
other_out.why: Money that went out other than for a party’s bill. The reason says where it counts.

sheet.title: Many entries at once
sheet.lede: One row is one entry. Tab moves to the next box, Enter to the row below. You can paste rows copied from Excel. Nothing is saved until you press Save, and every row gets the same checks as the form.
sheet.empty: Fill in at least one row first.
sheet.fromNew: Many entries at once? Type them in a sheet

party.indexLede: Red is what we still have to pay. Green is what we paid extra and will get back.
party.name: Party name
party.empty: No parties for this firm yet. Open a party below and add its first bill.
party.openOtherHint: Pick it to add its first bill or payment. A brand-new party?
party.noFirm: No firm is set up yet. Add one in Setup.
party.extraNote: To get back, or adjust in the next bill
party.billsHint: The opening balance comes first, then every bill from this party. Bill amount is with GST; the TDS is kept back and paid to the government, so the party is paid the bill amount less TDS.
party.noBills: No bills yet. The opening balance and every new bill will show here.
party.noPayments: No payments yet. Money paid to this party will show here.
party.addHint: Type in the rows like Excel: Tab and Enter move between boxes, and you can paste rows copied from Excel. Then press Save.
party.searchHint: Type a name to find a party…
party.noEntriesYet: No entries yet. Open to add the first bill.
party.clickHint: Click any row to open that party.
party.needSite: Add your sites first: every bill needs the site it was for.
party.needAccount: Add this firm's bank and cash accounts first: every payment needs where the money came from.

dashboard.title: {firm} – Dashboard
dashboard.lede: How much this firm still has to pay its parties, and how much it paid extra and will get back.
dashboard.top5: Top 5 parties – most remaining to pay
dashboard.chart: Each party: paid out of total
dashboard.chartHint: Bar length is what we owed in all. Green is paid, red is still to pay.

client.indexLede: Green is what we will still get. Red is what we received extra and have to give back.
client.name: Client name
client.searchHint: Type a name to find a client…
client.clickHint: Click any row to open that client.
client.empty: No client bills or receipts for this firm yet. Open a client below and add their first bill.
client.openOtherHint: Pick them to add their first bill or receipt. A brand-new client?
client.extraNote: To give back, or adjust in the next bill
client.billsHint: The opening due comes first, then running and stage bills given to this client. The client cuts TDS, retention and deposit; the rest is what they owe.
client.receiptsHint: Payments that came in from this client.

quick.nothingOwed: Nothing is due to {name} right now.

firm.switchLabel: Working in {firm}. Tap to switch firm.
firm.switchFailed: Could not switch firm. Try again.
firm.commonHint: Owner or supervisor cash: belongs to no firm.

stock.title: Stock
stock.lede: Pick a site and a period. The register shows, per material, what was there at the start, what arrived (added by the supervisor), what was used (from the daily reports) and what is left. Click a material to see its day-by-day movement.
stock.value: Value of stock left at the end (before GST)
stock.belowZero: More was reported used than arrived here. What arrived may not be added yet.
stock.none: Nothing in stock yet. Add what arrives at a site under “Arrived”.
stock.usedValue: Material used in this period (before GST)
stock.noneUsed: No material used in this period.
stock.noMoves: Nothing arrived or used in this period.

report.title: Daily report
report.lede: One site, one day: the work done, the material used, labour and staff, other costs, and what the day made. Supervisors fill it for their sites.
report.materialNote: Comes out of this site’s stock, at the rate typed on the line, else the average rate it arrived at
report.noSites: No sites given to you yet. Ask the office to add you to a site in People.
report.noWork: No work entered for this day yet. Add it below.
report.lines: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing entered yet} one {# line} other {# lines}}

use.addHint: Pick the material and type how much was used, or pick a combination work (PCC, RCC…) to add it as a group with all its materials inside, then type how much of the work was done today and its materials fill in (you can still change them). The rate fills in with the site’s average; change it if this lot cost different. Red means more than the stock shows: what arrived may not be added yet.
use.belowZero: More than this site’s stock. What arrived may not be added yet.

work.addHint: One block per activity. Write what was done and where on the site, pick the unit and type the rate. The measurement boxes follow the unit: M3 asks length × width × height, M2 length × width, Nos just the quantity. Use No. for how many alike (two walls: No. 2).
work.unitFirst: Pick the unit first. The measurement boxes appear for it.

report.noneUsed: No material entered for this day yet. Add it below.

errors.bad_quantity: Type the quantity, a number above zero like 0.45 or 483.
errors.need_measurement: This has no measurement. Type at least one, or remove it.
errors.bad_count: No. must be a number above zero, or left empty for 1.
errors.bad_length: Type the length, a number above zero like 4.3.
errors.bad_width: Type the width, a number above zero like 0.45.
errors.bad_height: Type the height, a number above zero like 2.8.
errors.bad_rate: The rate is not a rupee amount, like 600 or 2,500.
errors.not_removed: That line could not be removed. Supervisors can remove only their own lines, on the day they added them.
errors.already_marked: Someone here is already marked for this day, or present at another site. Open the day again to see who is left.
errors.need_description: Write what the cost was, like Tractor.
errors.pick_head: Pick what the cost was for.
errors.bad_ot: Type OT hours as a number from 0 to 16, like 2 or 1.5.
errors.ot_absent: OT can only be given on a day the person was present.
errors.staff_no_ot: Staff have a fixed monthly salary, so no OT.
errors.no_rate: This person has no rate in Setup → Workers and staff. Add it there first.
errors.bad_account: Choose an account you can pay from.
errors.future_paid: Money cannot be paid on a day that has not come.

report.costNote: Material, labour, staff and other costs
report.profitNote: Work done less the day’s costs
report.labourNote: {p} present · {a} absent. A worker’s day is 8 hours, OT paid per hour on top; staff are on a fixed monthly salary
report.noLabour: Nobody marked for this day yet. Mark who came below.
report.noWorkers: No workers or staff on the list for this site yet.
report.allMarked: Everyone on the list is marked for this day.
report.workerList: Add them in Setup → Workers and staff
report.noStaffPay: Staff salaries are not counted here.
report.otherNote: Tractor, labour colony, room, light, petrol: anything else the site cost today

labour.addHint: Tap P (present) or A (absent) for each person, and type OT hours worked past the 8-hour day. A worker’s day is 8 hours at their hourly rate in Setup, and each OT hour pays a day ÷ 8. Staff have a fixed monthly salary: no OT, nothing cut for leave; a day present counts a day’s share of it in this site’s costs. Anyone not marked is not saved.
labour.staffFixed: Staff have a fixed salary: no OT
labour.name: Name

other.addHint: Write what it was, pick what it was for, and type how many and the rate. Tractor is machine hire, not labour. Leave how many empty for 1.
other.head: What for

tds.title: TDS record
tds.lede: Every bill with TDS, with its rate, section and amount. TDS we deducted from parties is owed to the government. TDS clients deducted from our bills we can claim back.
tds.toClaim: TDS clients deducted, to claim back

gst.title: GST record
gst.lede: Every bill with GST. GST on bills from parties we can claim back. GST on our bills to clients is owed to the government. What is left to pay is the one less the other.
gst.owed: GST on our bills, owed to the government
gst.toClaim: GST on party bills, to claim back
gst.noneInMonth: No bills with GST in this month.

errors.duplicate: A material with this name is already in Setup. It may be switched off there: ask the office to switch it on.
errors.save_failed: Could not add the material. Try again.

salary.title: Salary
salary.lede: What each worker and staff member has earned, what is taken off and what is left to pay. Open a name for their salary slip and ledger.
salary.none: Nobody on this list yet. Add them in Setup → Workers and staff.
salary.name: Name
salary.ledeStaff: A fixed monthly salary, with no OT and nothing cut for leave. PF is cut unless switched off. Open a name to give an advance or take something off.
salary.ledeLabour: Type what you pay each worker a day, then their days and OT. The salary fills in (an OT hour is a day ÷ 8) and can be typed over. Pay per day carries on until you change it; saved months keep their salary. Nothing here comes from the daily report: its attendance and its rates are kept apart. PF is cut only when switched on.
salary.pfOff: Stop cutting PF for {name} from {month} on
salary.pfOnAll: Cut PF for everyone on this list from {month} on
salary.pfOffAll: Stop cutting PF for everyone on this list from {month} on
salary.beforeOwed: Add: left to pay from before
salary.moneyLede: An advance or salary paid says cash or bank; a deduction says why. Each counts in the period of its date, and what a month leaves carries into the next.
salary.noMoney: No advance, deduction or payment yet.
salary.openingLede: What was left with this person before you started using the app, for settling up. Type it once: it counts in the month you choose, as if it came from the month before, and carries on from there.

ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.pick: Pick a vendor, client or site
ledger.hint: Pick a vendor, client or site to see every entry in date order, with the balance after each one.
ledger.notFound: That vendor, client or site is not in this firm’s list.

vendor.dr: {firm} has paid {name} {amount} extra. {name} has to give it back, or it is adjusted in the next bill.

client.cr: {firm} has received {amount} extra from {name}. {firm} has to give it back, or it is adjusted in the next bill.

search.more: {count} more: keep typing to narrow the list

form.noCashAccount: This firm has no Cash yet. Add it in Setup → Bank and cash accounts.
form.noBankAccount: This firm has no bank account yet. Add one in Setup → Money accounts.

rentals.title: Rentals
rentals.lede: Things taken on rent for the sites, like shuttering plates, bamboo and props. The rent meter runs from the day they came: how many × rent per day × days. It stops on the day they go back. Add the bill number once the rent bill comes, to check which bill covers them.
rentals.linesOut: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing on rent} one {# line on rent} other {# lines on rent}}
rentals.clearHint: Clear the date if it was marked returned by mistake; the meter starts running again.
rentals.saved: Saved: {serial}. Its rent meter is running.

hints.rent_rate: For one item for one day, e.g. 0.75.
hints.rented_on: The meter starts on this day.
hints.bill_no: Can be added later, when the rent bill comes.

errors.not_removed: Could not remove it. Only the office, or whoever added it on the same day, can remove a line.

rentals.meterEmpty: Type how many and the rent per day to see what it costs.

clientBill.cutsHint: Leave empty what the client does not cut. TDS is worked out on the bill before GST.
clientBill.notePlaceholder: e.g. 3rd running bill, ground floor slab
clientBill.footHint: Every amount is worked out again when the bill is saved.

vendorBill.cutsHint: Leave empty if no TDS is deducted. Worked out on the bill before GST; you pay the party that much less.

assets.title: Assets
assets.lede: Tools and other things kept to reuse at any site, like axes and bowls (materials whose type is “Asset” in Setup). Supervisors add them when they arrive, and move them here when they go to another site. They are not a site’s stock.
assets.valueNote: At the average rate they arrived at
assets.atSites: {count, plural, =0 {At no site} one {At # site} other {At # sites}}
assets.none: No assets yet. Add them under “Arrived” when they reach a site.

errors.pick_all: Pick the asset and both sites.
errors.same_site: The two sites are the same.
errors.not_enough: That site does not have that many of this asset.

title.stock: Add stock that arrived at a site
title.assets: Add assets that arrived at a site

arrivals.hint: Leave the rate empty if you do not know it; then this line is not valued. A material not on the list? Type its name and pick “+ Add”.

errors.pick_all: Pick the material and the site.
errors.bad_rate: Type the rate for one unit, e.g. 350, or leave it empty.
errors.not_saved: Could not save. You can add only for your own sites.
errors.not_removed: Could not remove. A supervisor can remove their own line on the day it was added only.

mixes.hint: A work made of several materials, like PCC, RCC, plaster or tiles. Give its unit, then how much of each material 1 unit of it takes. On the daily report, picking this work adds these materials to the material used list.
mixes.name: Work
mixes.none: No combination works yet. Add PCC, RCC, plaster… below.

delete.title: Delete this work
delete.warning: It goes to the recycle bin and can be put back for 30 days. Daily reports already saved keep the work’s name and their materials. To stop offering it but keep it, switch it off instead.
delete.failed: Could not delete this work. Nothing was changed.

errors.need_name: Write the name of the work, like PCC.
errors.bad_quantity: Type how much 1 unit takes, a number above zero like 6.3 or 0.44.
errors.twice: This material is on the list twice.
errors.duplicate: A work with this name is already there.

labour.title: Labour payment
labour.lede: One line for each worker. Someone whose family works with them is paid through them: add the family from their page. Red is what we still have to pay. Green is what we paid extra, and it comes off the next salary.
labour.none: Nobody here yet. Add your first worker.
labour.name: Name
labour.rateFromHint: A changed salary counts from this month. Earlier months stay as they were.
labour.monthLede: Type each worker's totals for the month, with any advance and its reason. A family's members sit under its head: type each one's days and OT, and the family's advance on the head's line. An advance typed here comes off their salary but not out of a bank or cash; one given on the Pay tab is counted already, so do not type it again. Paid comes from the Pay tab. Salary, remaining and extra paid work themselves out. One double duty counts as two days, so days can pass the days in the month. A changed salary per day counts from this month on; earlier months keep theirs.
